items.question: In which year is the ratio of Product A to Product B closest to 1.4?

diagram.caption: Annual revenue (Rs crore) of two product lines, 2019-2024

items.explanation: Compute the ratio of Product A to Product B each year: 2019 is 1.50, 2020 is 1.56, 2021 is 1.18, 2022 is 1.60, 2023 is 1.38 and 2024 is 1.33. The target is 1.40, and 2023's 1.38 is the closest to it, nearer than 2024's 1.33 or 2019's 1.50. A solver who picks the year with the largest ratio, or the latest year, misses the comparison the question asks for.

items.set_title: DI2: Revenue of Two Product Lines
items.question: Which of the following statements CANNOT be true, given the data?

diagram.caption: Annual revenue (Rs crore) of two product lines, 2019-2024

options: Product A's total exceeds Product B's total by less than 320
The combined total in 2024 was the highest of any period
The grand total across all series and periods is 1590
Product A's total exceeds Product B's total by more than 320
Product A's share of the grand total is more than 53.5 percent
items.explanation: Four of the statements follow from the data, and only one does not. The false statement is the one that contradicts the computed totals, shares or growth rates in the data, while each of the other four can be checked directly against the figures given.

items.set_title: DI3: School Sections and Pass Rates
items.question: If Section C's strength rises to 100 students with the same pass rate and Section A's strength falls to 100 students with the same pass rate, what is the new total number of passes across all three sections?

diagram.caption: Students and pass rates in three sections of a school
diagram.content: A school has three sections. Section A has 120 students with a pass rate of 90%. Section B has 100 students with a pass rate of 80%. Section C has 80 students with a pass rate of 70%.

items.explanation: After the change, Section A has 100 students with a pass rate of 90 percent, giving 90 passes. Section B is unchanged at 100 times 0.80, which is 80. Section C has 100 students with a pass rate of 70 percent, giving 70 passes. The new total is 90 plus 80 plus 70, which is 240. The 244 option is the original total without the change, and the solver who applies the new strengths to the wrong sections gets a planted wrong answer.

items.set_title: DI3: School Sections and Pass Rates
items.question: If Section A's strength doubles with the same pass rate, which section then has the largest number of failures?

diagram.caption: Students and pass rates in three sections of a school
diagram.content: A school has three sections. Section A has 120 students with a pass rate of 90%. Section B has 100 students with a pass rate of 80%. Section C has 80 students with a pass rate of 70%.

options: Section A
Section B
Section C
Section A and Section C
All three groups have the same number
items.explanation: The failures are Section A: 120 times 10 percent, which is 12, Section B: 100 times 20 percent, which is 20, and Section C: 80 times 30 percent, which is 24. If Section A's strength doubles to 240 students, its failures double to 24, which ties Section C's 24. So Section A and Section C then jointly have the largest number of failures. The solver who answers from the original data picks Section C alone, and the solver who doubles the failure rate instead of the strength gets a planted wrong answer.

items.set_title: DI3: School Sections and Pass Rates
items.question: Which of the following statements CANNOT be true, given the data?

diagram.caption: Students and pass rates in three sections of a school
diagram.content: A school has three sections. Section A has 120 students with a pass rate of 90%. Section B has 100 students with a pass rate of 80%. Section C has 80 students with a pass rate of 70%.

options: The overall pass rate is 81.3 percent
Section C alone accounts for more than 40 percent of all failures
If Section B's strength rose to 120 with the same pass rate, the overall pass rate would exceed 82 percent
The total number of passes is 244
Section A's passes exceed Section B's by more than 25
items.explanation: The passes are 108, 80 and 56, totalling 244 out of 300 students, an overall pass rate of 81.33 percent, so the first statement is true. The failures are 12, 20 and 24, totalling 56, and Section C accounts for 24 of 56, which is 42.9 percent, more than 40 percent. If Section B's strength rose to 120, the totals would be 320 students and 260 passes, a rate of 81.25 percent, which does not exceed 82 percent, so the third statement cannot be true. Section A's passes exceed Section B's by 108 minus 80, which is 28, more than 25.

items.question: A briefing on the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics states that John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis shared the prize for demonstrating macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits. It also notes that the Aspect trio won in 2022 for quantum entanglement and the Agostini trio won in 2023 for attosecond pulses. Which pairing of laureates and work is correct?
options: Clarke, Devoret and Martinis; macroscopic quantum tunnelling
Aspect, Clauser and Zeilinger; macroscopic quantum tunnelling
Clarke, Devoret and Martinis; attosecond pulses
Agostini, Krausz and L'Huillier; macroscopic quantum tunnelling
Manabe, Hasselmann and Parisi; macroscopic quantum tunnelling
items.explanation: The candidate must match the trio to the work named for it. Only the first option pairs the 2025 trio with macroscopic quantum tunnelling. The second and fourth pair earlier trios with the 2025 work, the third keeps the right trio but gives it the 2023 work, and the fifth pairs the 2021 climate modelling trio with the 2025 work.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Jannik Sinner won the men's singles title at Wimbledon in 2025. He beat Carlos Alcaraz in the final. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Alcaraz won Wimbledon in 2025, beating Sinner in the final.
Alcaraz won Wimbledon in 2025, beating Djokovic in the final.
Djokovic won Wimbledon in 2025, beating Alcaraz in the final.
Sinner won Wimbledon in 2025, beating Djokovic in the final.
Sinner won Wimbledon in 2025, beating Alcaraz in the final, so Alcaraz was the runner-up.
items.explanation: The winner and the beaten finalist together fix the runner-up. The statement naming Sinner as winner, Alcaraz as the beaten finalist and therefore the runner-up gets all three right. Statements reversing the final, naming the wrong winner, or keeping the right winner but naming the wrong finalist each fail at least one fact.

items.question: A briefing on ISRO's December 2025 launch states three facts. The LVM3 rocket carried its heaviest payload to date. The satellite was BlueBird Block-2, weighing about 6,100 kg. It was launched for the United States company AST SpaceMobile. A report claims the heaviest LVM3 payload was a satellite built for SpaceX. Which correction follows from the briefing?
options: The claim is wrong: the satellite was BlueBird Block-2, launched for AST SpaceMobile, not SpaceX.
The claim is right: SpaceX was the customer.
The claim is wrong: the satellite was NISAR, launched for AST SpaceMobile.
The claim is wrong: the payload was the heaviest, but it was GSAT-20.
The claim is wrong: BlueBird Block-2 was launched for SpaceX.
items.explanation: The correction must fix both the satellite and the customer: BlueBird Block-2 for AST SpaceMobile. Only the first option does both. The second accepts the claim, the third and fourth keep the customer but name the wrong satellite, and the fifth keeps the satellite but names the wrong customer.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. In the Bihar Assembly election held in November 2025, the National Democratic Alliance won a decisive majority. Nitish Kumar became Chief Minister again. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: The Mahagathbandhan won a decisive majority and Nitish Kumar became Chief Minister again.
The National Democratic Alliance won a decisive majority and Tejashwi Yadav became Chief Minister.
The Bahujan Samaj Party won a decisive majority and Nitish Kumar became Chief Minister again.
The Jan Suraaj Party won a decisive majority and Tejashwi Yadav became Chief Minister.
The National Democratic Alliance won a decisive majority and Nitish Kumar became Chief Minister again.
items.explanation: The winning alliance and the returning Chief Minister must be matched. Only the fifth statement gets both right. The first and third name the wrong winning alliance, and the second and fourth name the wrong Chief Minister, even though the second keeps the right alliance.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Flesh by David Szalay won the Booker Prize in 2025. Flesh was published in 2025. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Orbital by Samantha Harvey won the Booker Prize in 2025 and was published in 2025.
Flesh by David Szalay won the Booker Prize in 2025 and was published in 2024.
James by Percival Everett won the Booker Prize in 2025 and was published in 2025.
The Bee Sting by Paul Murray won the Booker Prize in 2025 and was published in 2025.
Flesh by David Szalay won the Booker Prize in 2025 and was published in 2025.
items.explanation: The winning book, its author and its publication year must all agree. The statement naming Flesh by David Szalay, published in 2025, as the Booker winner gets all three right. Statements naming books that were shortlisted or won in other years, and the statement keeping the right book and author but moving its publication to 2024, each fail at least one fact.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. The Miss World 2025 pageant was held in Hyderabad. Opal Suchata Chuangsri of Thailand won the title. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: Miss World 2025 was held in Hyderabad and won by Opal Suchata Chuangsri of Thailand.
Miss World 2025 was held in Mumbai and won by Opal Suchata Chuangsri of Thailand.
Miss World 2025 was held in Hyderabad and won by Krystyna Pyszkova of the Czech Republic.
Miss World 2025 was held in New Delhi and won by Opal Suchata Chuangsri of Thailand.
Miss World 2025 was held in Bengaluru and won by Krystyna Pyszkova of the Czech Republic.
items.explanation: The host city and the winner must both be right. Only the first statement matches both. The second, fourth and fifth name the wrong host city, and the third keeps the right city but names the previous year's winner, Krystyna Pyszkova, instead of Chuangsri.

items.question: A briefing on BRICS states two facts. Indonesia joined BRICS as a full member in January 2025. Indonesia is the first Southeast Asian member of BRICS. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Indonesia is the first Southeast Asian member of BRICS, so no Southeast Asian country was a full member before January 2025.
Indonesia is the first Asian member of BRICS.
Indonesia joined as an observer, not as a full member.
Indonesia is the first African member of BRICS.
Argentina joined BRICS as a full member in January 2025.
items.explanation: Being the first member from a region means no country from that region was a member before, so only the first statement follows. The second widens the region from Southeast Asia to all of Asia, which the briefing does not support, the third downgrades full membership to observer status, the fourth moves Indonesia to the wrong continent, and the fifth names a country that never joined.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Rachin Ravindra was named Player of the Tournament at the ICC Champions Trophy 2025. He plays for New Zealand and was born in Wellington, New Zealand. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Ravindra plays for India and was born in Mumbai.
Ravindra plays for New Zealand and was born in Auckland.
Ravindra plays for Australia and was born in Sydney.
Ravindra plays for New Zealand and was born in Christchurch.
Ravindra plays for New Zealand and was born in Wellington.
items.explanation: The team and the birthplace must both be right. The statement naming New Zealand and Wellington gets both right. Statements naming the wrong team, and statements keeping the right team but naming the wrong New Zealand city, Auckland and Christchurch instead of Wellington, each fail at least one fact.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Time magazine named The Architects of AI as its Person of the Year for 2025. Donald Trump was Time's Person of the Year in 2024. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Donald Trump was Person of the Year in 2025 and The Architects of AI in 2024.
Taylor Swift was Person of the Year in 2025 and Donald Trump in 2024.
The Architects of AI were Person of the Year in 2025, succeeding Donald Trump from 2024.
Elon Musk was Person of the Year in 2025 and Donald Trump in 2024.
The Architects of AI were Person of the Year in 2025, succeeding Taylor Swift from 2024.
items.explanation: The two years must be ordered correctly with the right holder in each. Only the third statement does that: the Architects of AI in 2025 followed Trump in 2024. The first swaps the years, the second and fourth name the wrong 2025 holder, and the fifth names the wrong 2024 holder.

items.question: A briefing on the Census states two facts. The Government of India announced in 2025 that the next Census would include caste enumeration. Caste was last enumerated in the Census of 1931, which was held under British rule. A student says caste was last counted in independent India. Which reply is correct?
options: The student is right: caste was last enumerated in 1951.
The student is wrong: the last caste enumeration was in 1931, under British rule, more than ninety years ago.
The student is wrong: caste was last enumerated in 1941 under British rule.
The student is right: the 1961 Census enumerated caste.
The student is wrong: caste has never been enumerated in any Census.
items.explanation: The reply must give both the year and the ruler: 1931, under British rule, which is before independence, so the student is wrong. Only the second option does that. The first and fourth accept the student's claim with wrong years, the third keeps British rule but names the wrong Census year, and the fifth denies that caste was ever enumerated at all.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. 12th Fail won the Best Feature Film award at the 71st National Film Awards announced in 2025. It was directed by Vidhu Vinod Chopra. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: 12th Fail won Best Feature Film at the 71st National Film Awards and was directed by Vidhu Vinod Chopra.
Jawan won Best Feature Film at the 71st National Film Awards and was directed by Vidhu Vinod Chopra.
Animal won Best Feature Film at the 71st National Film Awards and was directed by Vidhu Vinod Chopra.
12th Fail won Best Feature Film at the 71st National Film Awards and was directed by Atlee.
Mrs Chatterjee vs Norway won Best Feature Film at the 71st National Film Awards and was directed by Vidhu Vinod Chopra.
items.explanation: The winning film and its director must be matched. Only the first statement pairs the right film with the right director. The second, third and fifth name the wrong film, and the fourth keeps the right film but names the director of Jawan, Atlee, instead of Chopra.

items.question: A gaming platform offers real-money rummy and free social games with no monetary stakes. After the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, passed in August 2025, what must the platform do?
options: Suspend its real-money games; it may continue its free social games
Suspend all its games, including the free social games
Continue its real-money games under a licence from the new Authority
Continue its real-money games but stop advertising them
Suspend its free social games and continue its real-money games
items.explanation: The Act places a complete prohibition on online money games, whether they are games of skill or games of chance, and there is no licensing route under which real-money games can continue, so the platform must suspend its real-money rummy. The prohibition covers offering the games themselves, not only advertising them, so stopping the advertising while continuing the games is not enough. E-sports and online social games with no monetary stakes are a different category: they are permitted and promoted, so the free social games may continue. Major platforms suspended their real-money games after the Act was passed, which is the response the law requires.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Aryna Sabalenka won the women's singles title at the US Open in 2025. She beat Amanda Anisimova in the final. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Coco Gauff won the US Open in 2025, beating Sabalenka in the final.
Sabalenka won the US Open in 2025, beating Anisimova in the final, so Anisimova was the runner-up.
Anisimova won the US Open in 2025, beating Sabalenka in the final.
Sabalenka won the US Open in 2025, beating Iga Swiatek in the final.
Naomi Osaka won the US Open in 2025, beating Anisimova in the final.
items.explanation: The winner and the beaten finalist together fix the runner-up. Only the second statement gets the winner, the finalist and the runner-up inference all right. The first, third and fifth name the wrong winner, and the fourth keeps the right winner but names the wrong finalist.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident. The incident took place in February 1922. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: Gandhi withdrew the movement after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in February 1922.
Gandhi withdrew the movement after the Chauri Chaura incident in February 1922.
Gandhi withdrew the movement after the Rowlatt Act in February 1922.
Gandhi withdrew the movement after the Chauri Chaura incident in April 1922.
Gandhi withdrew the movement after the Kakori conspiracy in February 1922.
items.explanation: The triggering incident and its month must both be right. Only the second statement gets both right. The first, third and fifth name different events from other years, and the fourth keeps the right incident but moves it to April, two months after it happened.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. The Great Stupa at Sanchi was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka, but the stone railing and the carved gateways were added under the Satavahana dynasty. Sanchi is located in Madhya Pradesh. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: The stone railing and gateways at Sanchi were added under the Gupta dynasty, in Madhya Pradesh.
The stone railing and gateways at Sanchi were added under the Chola dynasty, in Madhya Pradesh.
The stone railing and gateways at Sanchi were added under the Maurya dynasty, in Madhya Pradesh.
The stone railing and gateways at Sanchi were added under the Mughal dynasty, in Madhya Pradesh.
The stone railing and gateways at Sanchi were added under the Satavahana dynasty, in Madhya Pradesh.
items.explanation: The later dynasty and the state must both be right, and the later work must not be credited to Ashoka's own dynasty. Only the fifth statement gets both right. The first, second and fourth name dynasties from other periods and regions, and the third credits the additions to the Maurya dynasty, which commissioned the original stupa rather than the later stone work.

items.question: A briefing gives four pairings: The White Tiger with Aravind Adiga, Interpreter of Maladies with Jhumpa Lahiri, A Suitable Boy with Vikram Seth, and The Argumentative Indian with Amartya Sen. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: The White Tiger was written by Adiga and The Argumentative Indian by Sen, so the two books have different authors.
The White Tiger was written by Lahiri and Interpreter of Maladies by Adiga.
Interpreter of Maladies was written by Seth and A Suitable Boy by Lahiri.
A Suitable Boy was written by Adiga and The White Tiger by Seth.
The Argumentative Indian was written by Lahiri and Interpreter of Maladies by Sen.
items.explanation: Each option combines two pairings, so both halves must be checked. Only the first statement gets both pairings right and draws the correct consequence that the books have different authors. The other four each misassign at least one book, swapping authors between the pairs.

items.question: A briefing gives the years of four constitutional developments. Adoption of the Constitution, 1949. First Amendment, 1951. 42nd Amendment, 1976. 73rd Amendment, 1992. Which of the following statements about their order must be true?
options: The 73rd Amendment came before the 42nd Amendment.
The First Amendment came before the Constitution was adopted.
The Constitution was adopted first, then amended in 1951, 1976 and 1992 in that order.
The 42nd Amendment was the first amendment to the Constitution.
The 73rd Amendment came before the First Amendment.
items.explanation: The years must be ordered: 1949, 1951, 1976 and 1992. Only the third option gives that order. The first and fifth move the 1992 amendment earlier, the second puts an amendment before the document it amends, which is impossible, and the fourth mistakes the 1976 amendment for the first.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Kathak is a classical dance form of India. Kathak originates in Uttar Pradesh. Bhangra, Garba, Bihu and Lavani are folk dances, not classical forms. Which of the following is a classical dance form of India, and from which state does it originate?
options: Bhangra, from Punjab.
Garba, from Gujarat.
Kathak, from Uttar Pradesh.
Bihu, from Assam.
Lavani, from Maharashtra.
items.explanation: The answer must satisfy two conditions at once: the dance is classical, and its state of origin is named correctly. Only the third option does both. The other four name folk dances, so they fail the first condition even though the states named beside them are the right home states for those folk dances.

items.question: A briefing on the Green Revolution states three facts. M.S. Swaminathan led the introduction of high-yielding wheat and rice in India. Norman Borlaug is called the father of the Green Revolution. Verghese Kurien is associated with the White Revolution and Operation Flood. Which pairing of person and contribution is correct?
options: Swaminathan; high-yielding wheat and rice in India, while Borlaug is called the father of the Green Revolution.
Borlaug; high-yielding wheat and rice in India, while Swaminathan is called the father of the Green Revolution.
Kurien; the Green Revolution in India.
Swaminathan; Operation Flood.
Borlaug; Operation Flood.
items.explanation: The two roles must be kept apart: Swaminathan led the Indian work and Borlaug carries the title. Only the first option does both. The second swaps the two men, the third gives Kurien the Green Revolution instead of the White Revolution, and the fourth and fifth give Operation Flood to the wrong men.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. India hosted the G20 Summit in 2023, with the leaders' meeting held in New Delhi. The summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: India hosted the G20 Summit in 2023 and the summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration.
India hosted the G20 Summit in 2021 and the summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration.
India hosted the G20 Summit in 2022 and the summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration.
India hosted the G20 Summit in 2024 and the summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration.
India hosted the G20 Summit in 2023 and the summit adopted the Bali Declaration.
items.explanation: The year and the declaration must both be right. Only the first statement gets both right. The second, third and fourth move the summit to the wrong year, and the fifth keeps the right year but names the declaration adopted at the previous year's summit in Bali.
